ABSTRACT:

The E-Commerce Enterprise Web Application is a production-oriented, scalable digital commercial platform engineered utilizing Spring Boot 2.6.4, Hibernate ORM 5.6.5, and Neon Serverless PostgreSQL. Designed to eliminate the operational limitations of conventional offline stores and fragmented inventory systems, the application delivers an integrated e-commerce ecosystem catering to both public consumers and system administrators.

The architectural foundation follows the Model-View-Controller (MVC) paradigm, ensuring modular separation of concerns. The presentation layer utilizes high-performance JavaServer Pages (JSP) paired with Twitter Bootstrap 4 to render responsive, cross-platform user interfaces across desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers. Business logic is orchestrated through Spring Boot controllers and transaction-managed service layers, while the persistence tier utilizes a customized Hibernate SessionFactory connected securely to a cloud-hosted PostgreSQL database on Neon via SSL encryption.

Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is enforced through Spring Security, establishing clear operational boundaries between customer activities (user registration, catalog discovery, shopping cart aggregation, and instant checkouts) and administrative governance (category orchestration, real-time product updates, and customer directory auditing).

By migrating the relational database tier to Neon’s cloud-native serverless architecture, the system guarantees elastic compute scaling, automated connection pooling, and continuous high availability without the overhead of maintaining local database infrastructure. This comprehensive project report documents the entire system engineering lifecycle, encompassing requirement specifications, relational database schema models, architectural diagrams, output screenshots, code implementations, testing matrices, and future expansion roadmaps.

CHAPTER 1
INTRODUCTION

This chapter presents a comprehensive introduction to the E-Commerce Enterprise Web Application project. It discusses the core motivation, project aim, functional objectives, and technical background of the system, establishing the architectural context in which modern digital commercial portals operate.

1.1 PROJECT AIM AND OBJECTIVES

Aim: The primary aim of the E-Commerce Enterprise Web Application project is to engineer a secure, highly responsive, and fault-tolerant electronic marketplace that streamlines product catalog discovery, shopping cart management, and administrative inventory governance. The system leverages enterprise Java technologies and serverless cloud databases to deliver dependable electronic commerce operations.

Objectives:

  • Dynamic Catalog & Storefront: To design an interactive, accessible storefront interface enabling customers to discover categorized goods, inspect item details, and execute instant purchases seamlessly.
  • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): To implement robust security boundaries separating standard customer functions from administrative controls, preventing privilege escalation.
  • Administrative Management Hub: To construct a unified administrative dashboard for maintaining product categories, adding new products, modifying prices, and auditing user directories.
  • Custom Hibernate SessionFactory: To configure a dedicated Hibernate ORM persistence layer with explicit SessionFactory session management and transaction demarcation.
  • Cloud Serverless Data Persistence: To integrate Neon Serverless PostgreSQL with SSL encryption, ensuring high availability, automatic connection pooling, and cloud resilience.
3

1.2 BACKGROUND OF PROJECT

  • In today's globalized digital economy, electronic commerce has transformed from an auxiliary sales channel into the central pillar of retail commerce. Consumers expect uninterrupted, instantaneous access to comprehensive product inventories, transparent pricing structures, and intuitive checkout experiences accessible from any device. Legacy brick-and-mortar storefronts and standalone desktop bookkeeping tools suffer from physical geographic limitations, manual accounting errors, inventory desynchronization, and high operational maintenance overhead.
  • The evolution of modern enterprise web frameworks has established server-rendered MVC architectures as the industry standard for robust commercial web applications. The Spring Boot ecosystem provides comprehensive dependency injection, automated transaction management, embedded servlet containers, and declarative security configurations, significantly accelerating production deployment.
  • Concurrently, traditional on-premise relational database hosting has encountered severe challenges involving manual capacity provisioning, connection pool saturation, and local hardware single points of failure. The emergence of cloud-native serverless databases—such as Neon Serverless PostgreSQL—resolves these bottlenecks by separating storage from compute, offering instant auto-scaling, automated branching, and pooled SSL-encrypted connections.
  • The E-Commerce Enterprise Web Application project unites these advanced enterprise standards. By bridging Spring Boot 2.6.4, Hibernate ORM 5.6.5, and Neon Serverless PostgreSQL, the application provides a resilient, full-stack digital marketplace that models real-world enterprise software engineering.
4

CHAPTER 2
SYSTEM ANALYSIS

2.1 SOFTWARE REQUIREMENT SPECIFICATION

2.1.1 GENERAL DESCRIPTION:

  • The E-Commerce Enterprise Web Application is a web-based commercial shopping and inventory management platform designed to automate retail transactions. It allows consumers to register secure profiles, explore categorized inventories (Fruits, Vegetables, Bakery, Dairy, Meat, Drinks), examine product descriptions and stock counts, and execute cart checkout transactions in real time.
  • The system automates retail inventory operations through a centralized administrative portal. Authorized administrators can create new classification categories, add product listings with image specifications, update inventory stock levels, adjust pricing, and review registered customer accounts. Visual alerts and dynamic modals provide immediate operational feedback.
  • The platform is engineered to run seamlessly across all standard web browsers (Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Apple Safari). HTTP request dispatching is handled by an embedded Apache Tomcat 9 servlet container, while persistent records are securely stored within Neon Serverless PostgreSQL hosted on AWS cloud infrastructure.
  • System security is enforced through Spring Security authentication filters and BCrypt password encryption, safeguarding user credentials, preventing unauthorized access to administrative endpoints, and maintaining transactional consistency across all database operations.
5

2.1.2 SYSTEM OBJECTIVES

The central objective of the E-Commerce Enterprise Web Application is to establish a unified, secure, and responsive platform that coordinates commercial interactions between consumers and catalog administrators. The system is designed to eliminate operational bottlenecks, ensure data integrity, and guarantee uninterrupted availability.

Specific Objectives:

  • 1. Automated Product Catalog Management:
    Simplify the ingestion, updating, and taxonomy categorization of commercial goods via dynamic administrative interfaces, eliminating manual bookkeeping errors.
  • 2. Role-Based Identity and Access Management:
    Enforce strict role separation between standard customers (ROLE_NORMAL) and system administrators (ROLE_ADMIN), securing administrative routes from unauthorized access.
  • 3. Transactional Shopping Cart Operations:
    Provide dependable shopping cart aggregation with persistent state tracking in Neon PostgreSQL, allowing users to assemble items and execute checkout workflows.
  • 4. Serverless Cloud Database Resilience:
    Guarantee high availability, data durability, and automated compute scaling by migrating the persistence tier to Neon Serverless PostgreSQL over SSL connections.
  • 5. Responsive User Experience:
    Develop clean, accessible JSP templates styled with Twitter Bootstrap 4 that ensure intuitive shopping and administrative operations across all screen form factors.
6

2.1.3 SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS:

A. Hardware Requirements:

  • Processor: Intel Core i3 / AMD Ryzen 3 or higher (Quad-core 2.0 GHz recommended for application hosting).
  • RAM: Minimum 4 GB RAM (8 GB recommended for concurrent JVM, IDE, and browser execution).
  • Storage: Minimum 500 MB free disk space for application packages, compiled classes, and Maven dependencies.
  • Network: High-speed broadband internet connectivity for cloud database communication with Neon DB.
  • Display: Standard HD display (1366 x 768 or higher) for administrative portal monitoring and user browsing.

B. Software Requirements:

  • Operating System: Windows 10/11, Linux (Ubuntu/Debian), or macOS.
  • Runtime Environment: Java Development Kit (JDK) 17 LTS (Microsoft Build of OpenJDK 17).
  • Framework: Spring Boot Framework version 2.6.4 (Servlet stack, Spring MVC, Spring Security).
  • Persistence Framework: Hibernate ORM version 5.6.5 Final with custom SessionFactory configuration.
  • Database: Neon Serverless PostgreSQL (PostgreSQL 15 engine with SSL connectivity).
  • Build Tool: Apache Maven 3.8.6 with Maven Wrapper integration.
  • Web Server: Embedded Apache Tomcat 9.0.58.
  • Web Browser: Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, or Safari.

C. User Requirements:

  • End users must have access to a modern web browser and an active internet connection.
  • Customers require intuitive navigation to view items, filter categories, and manage checkout orders.
  • Administrators require secure access credentials to manage products, categories, and customer records.
7

2.2 SOFTWARE TOOLS USED :

  • Spring Boot 2.6.4: Core enterprise Java framework used for dependency injection, component scanning, auto-configuration, and orchestrating the MVC web tier.
  • Hibernate ORM 5.6.5: Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) framework providing automated schema synchronization, entity mapping, and SessionFactory transaction handling.
  • Neon Serverless PostgreSQL: Cloud-native database provider offering on-demand serverless PostgreSQL storage, pooled connectivity, and automated compute scaling.
  • Java 17 LTS: Modern, stable Long Term Support Java programming language runtime powering backend compilation and execution.
  • JavaServer Pages (JSP) & JSTL: Server-side template rendering technology used to dynamically generate responsive HTML views for customers and administrators.
  • Spring Security: Robust security framework providing authentication verification, CSRF safeguarding, and role-based authorization for administrative routes.
  • Apache Tomcat 9: Embedded servlet container handling HTTP network requests, session lifecycles, and servlet mappings.
  • Apache Maven 3.8.6: Project management and automated build automation tool managing libraries and application packaging.
  • Git & GitHub: Distributed version control system used for collaborative source code management, branching, and codebase versioning.
  • Visual Studio Code / IntelliJ IDEA: Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) utilized for enterprise Java programming, debugging, and terminal execution.
8

CHAPTER 5
SYSTEM TESTING

5.1 FUNCTIONALITY TESTING:

Functional testing is a critical dimension of enterprise software quality assurance, guaranteeing that every component and operation of the digital commerce platform functions in strict conformance with specified requirements. Below is an in-depth examination of functional testing methodology, lifecycle phases, and verification objectives:

What Is Functional Testing? Functional testing is a black-box verification technique where system capabilities are evaluated against explicit functional specifications. This methodology assesses what the system achieves in response to valid and invalid inputs, validating operational behavior without requiring direct visibility into internal code logic.

Key Objectives of Functional Testing:

  • Authentication & Role Enforcement: Verify that customer and administrator sessions are authenticated securely and role restrictions (ROLE_NORMAL vs ROLE_ADMIN) are strictly maintained.
  • Catalog & Cart Accuracy: Ensure that category queries accurately return matching inventory items and prices, weights, and stock quantities are correctly represented in carts.
  • Database Persistence & Integrity: Confirm that all user actions—such as product additions, category deletions, and address modifications—yield accurate modifications in Neon PostgreSQL.
  • Form Validation & CSRF Defense: Validate that mandatory inputs are enforced, duplicate usernames are rejected, and Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) tokens are validated.
26
Fig: 5.1 Functional Testing Lifecycle Workflow

Functional Testing Lifecycle Phases Breakdown:

Lifecycle Stage Engineering Activities Application Verification Target
Test Input Parameter definition & test data preparation Valid/invalid credentials, product form entries, category names
Functional Specifications Requirements mapping & boundary rules Spring Security role rules, unique constraints, FK dependencies
Test Cases Design Test matrix construction & scenario setup Equivalence partitioning, edge cases, session timeouts
Test Execution Manual execution & automated UI runs Headless Chrome navigation, endpoint submission, modal validation
Functional Testing Outcome assertion & database verification PostgreSQL table row validation, HTTP status code checks
27

5.2 Exception Testing Within Functional Testing :

While functional testing evaluates normal operational behavior, exception testing assesses how the system withstands anomalous, illegal, or adversarial inputs. This dimension ensures that the enterprise application maintains stability, preserves data integrity, and recovers gracefully when unexpected events occur.

Exception Testing Core Objectives:

  • Fault Tolerance: Ensure the application runtime does not crash or enter inconsistent states when handling invalid parameters or interrupted network calls.
  • Meaningful User Feedback: Replace cryptic stack traces with clear, actionable user-facing messages (e.g., "Invalid username or password" or "Username already taken").
  • Data Integrity Preservation: Ensure that failed transactional operations automatically rollback without corrupting database state in Neon PostgreSQL.
  • Security Enforcement: Verify that unauthorized access attempts to administrative endpoints are intercepted and securely redirected without exposing system internals.

Integration into Enterprise Lifecycle:

  • 1. Identification: Pinpoint high-risk modules (login forms, payment checkout, image uploads, database queries).
  • 2. Test Case Formulation: Construct negative tests (duplicate keys, SQL injection strings, null form fields).
  • 3. Execution & Monitoring: Observe Tomcat exception logs, Hibernate SQL statements, and browser responses.
  • 4. Resolution & Hardening: Implement declarative exception handling (`@ExceptionHandler`) and defensive validation.
28
Fig: 5.2 Exception Testing Lifecycle Workflow

Exception Testing Architecture Breakdown:

Workflow Stage Failure Injection Scenario System Recovery & Assertion
Test Input Malformed HTTP POST payloads or null form values Servlet container interceptor rejects malformed request
Functional Specifications Negative test contract definitions Defines expected HTTP error codes and redirect parameters
Test Cases Design Edge case parameterization & boundary stress Zero stock checkout, negative price submission, duplicate username
Functional Testing Controlled execution under failure injection Verifies that Spring Boot handles exception without process exit
Functional Exception Design Exception handler mapping Spring MVC maps exception to user-friendly alert banners
Result Comparison Outcome reconciliation with expected results Confirms zero orphan rows in Neon DB and clean recovery
29

5.3 EXAMPLES

The test execution matrix below summarizes representative functional and exception testing scenarios conducted across the e-commerce system:

Functional Area Exception / Scenario Expected Behavior Status
Customer Login User enters wrong password or non-existent username Displays "Please enter correct email and password" banner; denies session PASS
User Registration User attempts to register with already registered username SQL unique constraint caught; informs user that username is already taken PASS
Admin Login User enters invalid credentials on administrative gateway Displays "Invalid username or password. Please try again." alert banner PASS
Product Ingestion Admin leaves mandatory product name or price field blank HTML5 form validation triggers; submission prevented until fields filled PASS
Role-Based Security Regular user attempts direct URL access to /admin/products Spring Security intercepts request; redirects to /admin/login immediately PASS
Category Modal Admin opens "Add Category" modal and submits new category Category saved to Neon DB; view reloads showing updated taxonomy list PASS
Category Update Admin modifies category title via #exampleModalCenter2 modal Executes SQL UPDATE in Neon DB; reflects updated title instantly PASS
Order Placement Customer clicks "Buy Now" on catalog product Renders instant checkout confirmation; confirms delivery details PASS
Cloud DB Resilience Transient network disconnection during database operation Hibernate rolls back active transaction; preserves database consistency PASS

CHAPTER 6
CONCLUSION

  • The E-Commerce Enterprise Web Application project has successfully accomplished its primary mission: engineering a dependable, scalable, and intuitive electronic marketplace platform that bridges consumer convenience with administrative operational efficiency. Built upon enterprise Java standards—specifically Spring Boot 2.6.4, Hibernate ORM 5.6.5, and Neon Serverless PostgreSQL—the system demonstrates end-to-end software engineering excellence.
  • Throughout the project lifecycle, our team designed and implemented essential commercial modules, including dynamic JSP storefront rendering, categorized product browsing, transactional shopping cart aggregation, role-based authentication and authorization, and comprehensive administrative inventory governance. Each module was engineered according to the Model-View-Controller architectural pattern, ensuring loose coupling, maintainability, and high code readability.
  • A key architectural milestone was the migration of the database layer to Neon Serverless PostgreSQL. By leveraging cloud-native PostgreSQL 15 over secure SSL connections, the platform achieved automated connection pooling, on-demand compute scaling, and cloud data durability, completely removing the dependency on vulnerable local database installations.
  • Rigorous functional and exception testing confirmed that the application performs reliably across diverse operational scenarios. Security barriers reliably protect administrative routes against unauthorized access, database unique constraints prevent record duplication, and automated transaction rollbacks safeguard financial and inventory integrity during unexpected network disruptions.
31

CONCLUSION (CONTINUED)

  • This project has also served as an invaluable collaborative learning experience, reinforcing practical proficiencies in enterprise full-stack development, serverless cloud integration, Spring Security filter chains, Hibernate SessionFactory management, and automated testing methodologies. The practical problem-solving skills acquired during production debugging—such as resolving PostgreSQL driver integrations and automating headless browser rendering—have laid a robust foundation for future software engineering endeavors.
  • Future Scope and Roadmap: Although the current implementation provides a complete, production-ready e-commerce core, several high-impact enhancements are envisioned for future iterations:
  • 1. Payment Gateway Integration: Incorporating third-party payment APIs (such as Razorpay, Stripe, or PayPal) with webhook idempotency to enable automated card, UPI, and digital wallet payment verification.
  • 2. Automated Email & SMS Dispatch: Integrating Spring Mail and SMS notification services to deliver automated order invoices, tracking details, and security reset tokens to registered consumers.
  • 3. AI-Powered Product Recommendations: Implementing machine learning recommendation algorithms based on customer purchase history to deliver personalized cross-selling and up-selling recommendations.
  • 4. Containerization & Cloud CI/CD: Packaging the application into multi-stage Docker containers and configuring continuous integration/continuous deployment pipelines with Kubernetes for automated multi-region deployment.
